title: Agentic Development Security — Ezra Tanzer, Snyk
talk_summary: Snyk describes securing agent-generated code, agent supply chain (MCP servers/skills), and agent actions, and shows a concrete shift from MCP-server-plus-rules to asynchronous Python hooks that scan on file writes and only surface newly introduced issues at session stop. They also demo local visibility/audit of agent commands, file access, and cost, plus deterministic pre-tool-execution guardrails that block risky actions like reading secrets.

takeaways.technique: Async post-write scan hooks with session-stop fix loop
takeaways.what_they_do: A Python hook fires asynchronously on each agent file write/modify, runs a CLI scan, writes only newly introduced issues to a temp file, and at session stop triggers a fix-and-validate loop only if new issues exist.

Hooks intercept pre-tool execution in near real time, assess risk, and either steer (e.g., redact secrets/PII and proceed) or ask the human; destructive shell commands or out-of-scope directory access trigger asks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're relying right now from an implementation perspective on hooks that can intercept kind of a pre-tool execution in near real time

takeaways.technique: Audit log of agent commands, file access, and cost
takeaways.what_they_do: A local watcher records every command an agent runs, files it reads/writes (flagging heavy reads with no edits), web pages hit, MCP tools used, and per-agent cost, giving traceability.

takeaways.technique: Inventory and risk-score installed MCP servers and skills
takeaways.what_they_do: Auto-discovers MCP servers and skill files on a machine, retrieves tool descriptions, analyzes them for risk, and surfaces a risk score per component.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one in 12 developers in this group had an MCP server where there is either a high or critical severity finding
takeaways.numbers: 1 in 12 developers had a high/critical finding in an MCP server; 1 in 8 of ~4,000 skills had a critical issue; 76 malicious payloads found

takeaways.technique: Prefer hooks over rules/skills for enforcement
takeaways.what_they_do: They found rule files were sometimes ignored by agents and added latency/tokens; hooks made the workflow deterministic and removed latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Agents sometimes ignored the rule files. Uh scan execution did add latency at the end of its run

takeaways.technique: Only surface newly introduced issues to the fixing agent
takeaways.what_they_do: The temp-file diff of new-vs-existing findings means the agent context only receives newly introduced problems, not the whole backlog.
takeaways.evidence_quote: newly introduced issues are the only thing that's being surfaced to that agent context, the context window doesn't get any unnecessarily unnecessary bloat
